items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: In the meantime Bob Crosby was playing his tune 'Muskrat Ramble' all the time, you know, and he wrote it.

ctx.x: Yeah, and from then on -- I told him, "Now, get your band together now. Get your band that you brought up here from New Orleans." He brought a band here from New Orleans, you know. I said, "Oh, bring them and rehearse them." I said, "Some people would want to give you a job."

So he did that. In the meantime Bob Crosby was playing his tune 'Muskrat Ramble' all the time, you know, and he wrote it. So I asked him one day, I says, "Hey, 'Dud,' isn't that your tune?" He said, "Yes." I said, "Are you getting any royalties?" He said, "No." I said, "Well, who published it?" He said, "Melrose." I said, "Melrose?" He said, "Yeah."
I said, 'Well, don't you ever hear from him?' He says, 'No.' 'Well, okay, we're going to see about that.' So I take him down to Vine Street where publishing row is, you know, --

items.title: Barney Bigard Interview, 1969-07-25
items.q: Because when Crosby had, remember, he had this band? Bobcats.

ctx.x: Hi Bill, this is Floyd Levin in Los Angeles. This is the 25th of July 1969 and shortly I expect Barney Begard over, at which time I will supply the questions and hopefully he'll come up with some of the answers to help you on your quest for information about Jelly Roll Morton. Okay, we've just played the Victor Trio session, Barney. I assume that you have some memories about that session. Yeah, I was really surprised. I thought I played more than I do now. That's going back, what, 40 years? Yes, it is. Could you…
. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. That's okay. You can cut that off. One. Two. You see, if you count and then pick back the notes up, it screws you up. Yeah. ¶ Thank you.
